items.title: Joseph "Fan" Bourgeau Interview, 1972-09-13
items.q: Me and his wife, Miss Alexander, she was a piano player... We used to play all in Vic Harvey, all around there. Four-piece band.

ctx.x: That's strange because violin had gone out.
Gone out, but none of you were violin players like Peter was. And like P-Rone. You remember P-Rone?
I heard him on the records.

items.title: Joseph "Fan" Bourgeau Interview, 1972-09-13
items.q: I used to play with him too. ... Peter Rabbit. ... He was playing at the Petroleum Club.

ctx.x: That was real interesting what you were saying about Gayno.

Gayno never had a band. I was the one who knew Gayno how to play in a band. He played after me because I was probably playing this, Johnny Sensei was the first guy who showed me how to play the guitar. And then I switched from guitar to banjo. Johnny Sensei used to play with us too on the Airline Highway. In the 4900, he was on the Airline Highway. We played there. He had a little trumpet called Caledon. He said, I'll be there when you're going to get there. I said, okay. I had playing with him. I had Lawrence's…
What did he play? He played Coney. You mean the guy that was any kind of Blue? No, it wasn't a kind of Blue. No, it wasn't no kind of Blue.

items.title: Joseph "Fan" Bourgeau Interview, 1972-09-13
items.q: He's got a son who lives in Baltimore, Maryland. What's his son's name? Well, we call him P.J. Alexander. Now what that P.J. stands for, I don't know. Well, it could be Peter Junior.

ctx.x: Yeah, he died. He's got a son who lives in Baltimore, Maryland. What's his son's name? Well, we call him P.J. Alexander. Now what that P.J. stands for, I don't know. Well, it could be Peter Junior.
